title: Cancellation path silently swallows CancelledError and skips the structured failure log when the started worker raises after the request is cancelled
description: In run_blocking_with_response_timeout's `except asyncio.CancelledError` branch, the drain loop `while not blocking_task.done(): await asyncio.shield(blocking_task)` only catches asyncio.CancelledError (to re-loop on re-cancellation). If the already-started worker thread finishes by raising an ordinary (non-cancellation) exception, `await asyncio.shield(blocking_task)` re-raises that worker exception. Because it is not an asyncio.CancelledError, it is not caught by the `except asyncio.CancelledError: continue` arm: it propagates out of the while loop AND out of the entire `except asyncio.CancelledError` block. Two consequences follow: (1) the trailing bare `raise` (which re-raises the original CancelledError) is never reached, so the in-flight request cancellation is suppressed and converted into a domain exception, violating the asyncio structured-concurrency contract that a coroutine catching CancelledError must re-raise it; upstream cancellation/limiters may then treat the task as 'failed' rather than 'cancelled'. (2) `_drain_background_future_result(blocking_task)` is skipped, so the dedicated structured `route_work_background_failed` error log for a worker that failed after cancellation is never emitted (the failure is only visible as whatever exception type the caller did not expect). This contradicts the project's 'fail loudly / observable failures' principle. The normal-return cancellation path (worker returns a value) is correct and is the only behaviour the existing test test_run_blocking_with_response_timeout_cancellation_waits_for_worker exercises; the worker-raises-after-cancel branch is untested.
evidence: Lines 51-58: `except asyncio.CancelledError:` then `while not blocking_task.done(): try: await asyncio.shield(blocking_task) except asyncio.CancelledError: continue` then `_drain_background_future_result(blocking_task)` then `raise`. asyncio.shield's returned awaitable propagates the inner task's result/exception unless the OUTER await is cancelled; so a worker raising e.g. ValueError makes `await asyncio.shield(blocking_task)` raise ValueError, which the `except asyncio.CancelledError` arm does not catch -> escapes both the while loop and the outer except block, bypassing `_drain_background_future_result(blocking_task)` and the `raise`. Contrast the timeout branch (lines 47-50), which deliberately routes background failures through `blocking_task.add_done_callback(_drain_background_future_result)` so a late worker exception IS logged. The cancellation branch lacks that guarantee. The drain helper itself (lines 61-70) is the only place the `route_work_background_failed` structured error is produced.
